newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UCB seen making good in first half.
newsitem.headline: UCB seen making good in first half.

text.p: Analysts expect Belgian drugs, fine chemicals and plastic films group UCB to deliver a 30 to 35 percent increase in profits in the first half of 1997 when it releases the figures on Wednesday.

But the impact of the expected good news on the company's shares will be limited. Some analysts rate the stock a 'hold', saying it is expensive at current levels. Others, noting the share is fully-valued, say it is a 'speculative buy' at best.

An earnings increase in the 30 to 35 percent bracket would be perfectly in line with company forecasts made at the annual general meeting, leaving the market hoping for a surprise to give the share new potential.
That surprise could take the form of better than expected earnings, but also an explanation for the mystery buying which drove the stock to record heights around the middle of July.
At the time talk centred on a London broker acting on behalf of an aggressive buyer ready to pay whatever it took for UCB. But there were takeover rumours too.
Belgian bulk chemicals maker Solvay, which has its eye on expanding more aggressvely into pharmaceuticals, was named as well as Johnson & Johnson and Pfizer, both of the U.S.
Solvay denied the rumours, branding the story an old chestnut.
As UCB's marketing partner in the U.S. for the Belgian company's star anti-allergy drug Zyrtec, Pfizer has a link to UCB. There is no known connection between UCB and Johnson.
Analysts will scrutinise the first half report for clues as to how UCB will book a surplus of the order of one billion francs ($26.4 million) following a share sale by one of its subsidiaries.
UCB chief executive officer Georges Jacobs is also expected to comment on the closely-held share's runaway performance.

The stock began to take off at the end of May, when it was at 95,600 francs, peaking at 153,000 on July 17. It was at 140,600 at midday on Tuesday, still 45,000 francs above the level seen almost two month ago.
Gert De Mesure at Bank Delen is holding onto a 'long-term buy'. "It is a security we are keeping in our portfolios."

Brokers Corluy, saying the stock is a 'hold' or a 'market performer', adds it can still be bought, especially if UCB lives up to the expectations. "A price/earnings ratio of 27 could be justified if profits go up by 30 percent," it said.

Analysts were loath to forecast the half year figures. Full year 1997 earnings per share range from 4,160 to 4,180 francs. Depending on analysts' calculation methods, the comparable 1996 EPS figure is 3,054 francs or 3,143.

Six months earnings will not be an exact half of the full year figures since the first half includes the spring season in the western hemisphere, which is peak hayfever time and accordingly a top-selling period for UCB's Zyrtec.
Ordinary pre-tax profits, before exceptionals, rose 31 percent in the first half of 1996 to 2.93 billion francs.
Drugs are UCB's largest contributor to pre-tax profits.
Data from the U.S. show second quarter sales of Zyrtec there rose by 94 percent to $70 million. The company forecasts total 1997 sales of Zyrtec in the U.S. of $250 million.
